comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. buildCredentialBadge() in dom.js is a textbook single-responsibility utility: pure DOM construction, no side effects, no coupling to view state. The BEM-style modifier classes (.credential-badge--set / .credential-badge--none) and the aria-label attributes are correct and idiomatic.

MAINTAINABILITY: The conditional in buildCredentialBadge() uses a simple truthiness check (`if (credentialId)`). This correctly handles null, undefined, empty string, and 0 as the 'no credential' state — all of which the QA agent verified via edge-case tests. The contract is well-documented in the JSDoc. No change needed.

BEST PRACTICES: The project-detail.js call site uses `buildCredentialBadge(repo && repo.credentialId)` (line 271). This is correct defensive coding — `repo` may be undefined when a project references a repository ID not present in the global repo list. The short-circuit produces `undefined`, which buildCredentialBadge() handles as the --none state. The pattern is clear and consistent.

PERFORMANCE: No concerns. Badge construction is O(1) DOM work per row. No innerHTML, no string parsing, no layout thrash. textContent assignment is the correct and safe approach confirmed by QA's XSS edge-case test.
